mathematical_results: Exact derivative coupling: at fixed aperture, E_even_second(theta)=-36pi^2 E_odd(theta). Full regularized transport yields one actual primitive B with B_second=rho(t)dt+sum Lambda(q)/sqrt(q) delta_logq and Q_even=(36pi^2/L)integral E_odd(s)B(L(1-s))ds.

Native pole neutrality makes replacing B by B-8cosh(t/2) exact in this pairing. The new second derivative is the signed prime/pole discrepancy plus the retained Arch density. The apparent positive curvature does not give an independent sign after this subtraction.

For every actual aperture the odd source profile has both signs against positive convex hinges. The actual first prime atom makes P0^2 B an indefinite distribution. These are precise failures of generic positivity inferences, not a counterexample to a possible inequality for the single prescribed complete pairing.

Both complete unsigned prime charges have the SAME leading scale c exp(L/2)L^-r (r=9 even,7 odd), with c>0. Complete positive Selberg charges have an additional factor2L. Their signed cancellation is retained; neither individual charge is polynomially bounded.

The complete fixed-K3 signed energies have both logarithmic excursion rates equal to the actual native zero-displacement supremum Theta. In particular an off-line zero rules out every eventual polynomial lower bound. This extends the previously reviewed aperture/Landau derivation; it supplies no unconditional bound.

The complete aperture differential relation retains an actual source forcing whose off-line singular coefficient is nonzero. A polynomial suppression of this forcing cannot justify deleting it or treating the system as a homogeneous coercive ODE.
